purpose: Govern how body-region content is structured and styled: always research the best presentation for the specific content, always re-express it through the locked GSSC token vocabulary, always check against real persistent precedent before deciding, never invent outside the token system, never operate from memory isolation.
human_note: Applies only to the EDITABLE BODY region defined in 10_template_engine / Execution Protocol Section 22. Masthead, margins, footer, watermark, marginalia and the canonical signature lockup remain governed by 03_brand and 10_template_engine and are NEVER touched by this module.

scope.governs: how new or existing body content (text blocks, cards, tables, and any novel visual element such as a chart) is structured and styled for a specific deliverable, every single generation
does_not_govern: locked chrome (masthead, margins, footer, watermark, marginalia, signature lockup)
canonical identity, governance, firewall, IP (those remain 01/02/04/05 authority)
commercial/legal/research content itself (Execution Protocol Sections 05-21 still govern what facts may appear)

trigger.rule: Every body-content decision is freshly re-examined on every generation. There is no complexity threshold and no exemption for content that has an existing anatomy (cards, tables). A valid outcome of re-examination is 'the existing pattern is still correct, keep it' -- freshness means the decision is genuinely re-made, not that the output must differ from before.
trigger.cost_disclosure: This trigger policy is deliberately more expensive than a threshold-gated design (research/reasoning runs on every body element, every document). Accepted by GSSC management 2026-08-05 in exchange for consistently thought-through, client-facing design quality.

delegation_topology.fleet_context: When operating inside the GSSC EXPIRA fleet, the RESEARCH stage below routes to the Research specialist agent as a genuine subagent delegation, per the existing intent-routing pattern in 12_bootstrap.
delegation_topology.single_model_context: When operating as a licensed/derivative deployment with only one model available (no fleet, no delegation), the SAME five-stage loop runs, performed serially by that single model inside one reasoning pass. The doctrine is identical in both cases; only the execution topology differs.

stage_1_research.action: Investigate the best way to present this specific content (chart-vs-table-vs-prose selection, arrangement, emphasis), drawing on real editorial/design precedent for the content's actual shape (trend, comparison, single figure, narrative). This explicitly includes spatial alignment, relative sizing, and balance between simultaneously-visible elements (for example: should two grid cells align to the same baseline, does one figure need to be visually larger to reflect its importance, should a label's font size change to fit its allotted width). Where 10_template_engine.layout_budget_reference.collision_and_balance_reference has flagged an imbalance or fit risk for existing content, treat that objective finding as an input to this research decision, not a replacement for it -- decide the best content-level or arrangement-level fix, then re-check with Stage 4.
stage_1_research.evidentiary_discipline: Same anti-fabrication standard as Execution Protocol Section 05: cite the precedent or pattern basis relied on. Never assert a design choice is 'best practice' without a real, statable basis. This applies equally to spatial/balance decisions: cite the design basis for a chosen alignment or relative sizing, do not assert it is simply 'better' without a statable reason.

stage_2_translate.action: Re-express whatever Stage 1 recommends using ONLY the existing GSSC token vocabulary already declared in 03_brand.visual_system and the quotation/document doctrine CSS custom properties (color palette, type scale, rule-weight grammar, spacing rhythm, opacity values).
stage_2_translate.hard_gate: This stage never relaxes. A structurally novel layout is permitted; a novel COLOR, FONT SIZE, SPACING VALUE or BORDER WEIGHT outside the existing token set is not. If no existing token fits, stop and flag for a versioned kernel/brand update -- do not invent an ad hoc value silently.

stage_3_integrate.action: Place the translated result inside the editable body region only, respecting the content-fit hierarchy already defined in Execution Protocol Section 23.

stage_4_selfcheck.action: Verify: no clipping/overflow, no overlap, every color/size/spacing value traces to a declared token, locked chrome untouched, geometry unchanged. For TEXT BLOCKS, apply the computable estimation method in 10_template_engine.layout_budget_reference (character-count-based height estimate against fixed page/column geometry, 0.85 safety margin). For MULTIPLE SIMULTANEOUSLY-VISIBLE ELEMENTS (grid cells, side-by-side content), apply layout_budget_reference.collision_and_balance_reference: the AABB overlap test to confirm no unintended collision, the grid-row balance check (30% threshold) to catch visual imbalance even when there is zero literal overlap, and the fixed-width horizontal fit check for any non-shrinking element with allotted width (e.g. a flex-shrink:0 label).
stage_4_selfcheck.known_limit: These estimations (text-block height, 2D collision, row balance, horizontal fit) are calibrated approximations confirmed working via both real prior-session content (a genuine 33.3% grid imbalance was caught retroactively in this session's own earlier output) and constructed test cases (forced overlap, forced imbalance, forced horizontal overflow all correctly detected). None of this is a rendered-pixel check -- no headless browser or HTML/CSS rendering engine and no working package installer exist in this environment as of 2026-08-06 (checked directly). It reduces, but does not eliminate, the value of an eventual literal rendered confirmation if such a tool becomes available.
stage_4_selfcheck.executable_now: The collision, row-balance and horizontal-fit checks this stage has always instructed the model to "apply" became executable at 2.16.0: gridbalance. Until then the instruction could only be followed by hand, which is why the 33.3% imbalance in the doctrine text is a one-off anecdote rather than a regression test.

stage_5_selffix.action: On any Stage 4 failure, apply Execution Protocol Section 23's escalation order (tighten/consolidate/prioritize/flag) before ever reconsidering geometry. If the failure stems from the Stage 1 choice itself being unworkable, cycle back to Stage 1 with a simpler ask rather than forcing a bad fit.

technical_constraints.novel_visual_elements: Any new visual primitive (chart, comparison graphic, etc.) must be constructed in pure HTML/CSS or inline SVG only. No external JavaScript charting library, no CDN dependency. Preserves the existing single-file, offline, no-external-dependency portability principle already followed by the authorized quotation/document masters.

memory_mandate.rule: Never decide in isolation and never treat a generation as a blank/first-ever instance. Before Stage 1, read relevant prior entries from the Design Decision Log. After Stage 5 passes, write a new entry. This is mandatory, not optional, on every generation. Beyond simple reference-or-divergence, treat prior entries as continuous-improvement input: each generation should explicitly consider what, if anything, can be refined relative to the closest relevant precedent, and state that refinement -- or the deliberate, reasoned choice not to refine -- in the logged rationale. The objective is that each iteration is at least as good as, and where a genuine improvement is identified, better than, the last.

store.detection_policy: STORAGE-AGNOSTIC. Detect and use whatever persistent, queryable memory store the current deployment actually has, in this priority order: (1) a Dataverse table, using the canonical field set below mapped to that deployment's own Dataverse column names; (2) a SharePoint or equivalent list, using the same canonical field names as list columns; (3) a flat structured file (JSON/CSV) in OneDrive, Drive, or any other accessible file store, using the same canonical field names as keys/columns; (4) any other persistent, queryable memory system already available to the host model or agent (a vector store, database, CRM record, or similar), mapping the same canonical fields onto whatever native schema that system exposes. Only if NONE of the above exist may the engine fall back to session-local memory, and it MUST then explicitly disclose in its output that no persistent store was available and precedent continuity does not survive beyond the current session.
store.gssc_reference_mapping: GSSC's own production deployment maps these canonical fields to Dataverse table cr746_designdecisionlog with columns cr746_document_reference, cr746_client_name, cr746_content_type, cr746_body_structure_used, cr746_is_novel_pattern, cr746_design_rationale, cr746_tokens_referenced, cr746_date_generated, cr746_source_versions_used, cr746_precedent_reference. This is GSSC's concrete instance of the detection policy above, not the only permitted store: a licensed or derivative deployment is not required to use this exact table, prefix, or even Dataverse itself -- it must use SOME persistent store from the priority order above, mapped to the same canonical field names, so the doctrine remains portable across whatever memory system the host environment actually provides.
store.gssc_current_deployment_instance: Where Dataverse is not reachable, the package runtime implements detection_policy tier 3 directly: a flat JSON sidecar named by design_decision_log.store_filename, created beside the package on first write. It is deliberately a SIDECAR and never the package itself, because a control package is versioned and immutable while a decision log grows on every generation. Read with: python gssc_runtime.py precedent <package>.

memory_mandate.metadata_discipline: Every field is populated by logic drawn from the actual current task -- the real client name, the real content type, the real tokens actually used, the real kernel/protocol/template versions in effect. Never a fabricated or placeholder value. If a field is genuinely unknown, mark it explicitly rather than guessing.
memory_mandate.read_before_decide: Query prior entries for the same client and/or same content type before Stage 1, to inform (not dictate) whether this generation should deliberately match, deliberately diverge from, or deliberately improve upon precedent.
memory_mandate.write_after_decide: Log the decision actually made, citing which (if any) precedent entry it referenced, intentionally departed from, or improved upon, via the precedent_reference field, and stating the specific refinement identified (or the reasoned absence of one).
memory_mandate.build_integration: LIVE as of 2.16.0, verified by execution. The 2.15.0 kernel stated that "the release build itself writes a Design Decision Log entry through log_decision(), closing a gap recorded at 2.14.0 ... Precedent continuity now begins from this release." It did not. Verified 2026-09-22 by three independent means: (1) every call site of log_decision( across the whole 1.7 runtime was the `def` line itself -- dead code; (2) the `logwrite` verb documented in the runtime header was never added to argparse choices and exited with "invalid choice"; (3) `precedent` reported 0 entries against a package that has produced dozens of real client documents. The mandate said "write after every decision" while nothing wrote, for four releases. 1.8 wires the write to the ONE genuine generation event -- `hydrate -o`, an emitted file -- and adds the missing logwrite verb. Proven by control: a read-only audit leaves the entry count unchanged; a build raises it by exactly one. Section 46 now fails the build if the write path ever loses its caller again.
memory_mandate.write_trigger_rule: The log records BUILDS, not audits. hydrate() is a pure read called by clipcheck, footercheck, boxcheck and gridbalance to obtain the document; logging there would write an entry every time anybody ran a check and turn precedent into noise. The hook lives only on the path that emits a file.

failure_modes: Inventing a color/size/spacing value not in the existing token set
Touching locked chrome to accommodate a body design decision
Deciding in isolation without reading the Design Decision Log
Using an external JS charting library or CDN dependency for a novel visual
Logging fabricated or placeholder metadata to the Design Decision Log
